newsitem.title: USA: US lawmakers ask Clinton to ease Colombia sanctions.
newsitem.headline: US lawmakers ask Clinton to ease Colombia sanctions.

text.p: Nine U.S. lawmakers urged President Bill Clinton on Saturday to ease sanctions on Colombia one week before an annual evaluation of countries the United States believes are not doing enough to fight drug trafficking.
Clinton punished Colombia last year for failing to stem the flow of illegal drugs by cutting off most U.S. aid and support for loans from multilateral financial institutions.
In a letter, the lawmakers pressed Clinton to restore assistance for supplies and training to support anti-drug efforts in the South American country.
"At the very least, we ask that you seriously consider immediate steps to remove obstacles to key anti-drug support," said the letter, dated Feb. 21 and released on Saturday.
Clinton has to grade Colombia, Mexico and 30 other countries by March 1 in the certification process, Washington's annual evaluation of other governments' fight against drugs.

Some countries on the blacklist are not subject to sanctions for national security reasons, and the lawmakers pressed Clinton to use that waiver or "specifically allow Foreign Military Financing to the counternarcotics effort in Colombia."

The lawmakers, led by Republicans Representative Dan Burton, chairman of the House of Representatives Government Reform and Oversight Committee, Representative Benjamin Gilman, chairman of the chamber's International Relations Committee, said they remained committed to fighting drug trafficking.

"We will continue to urge the Colombians to finish work on a tough sentencing law that is progressing in their congress," their letter said. They said they would press Colombia to amend its constitution to allow extradition of drug traffickers and to fully implement a law allowing seizure of their assets.
